title: Claim is not idempotent over an existing same-assignee assignment
description:
`jit issue claim <id> <assignee>` hard-fails with "Issue is already assigned" even when the existing assignee is the claimant, so an assignment cannot be promoted into a real claim without losing claim semantics.

## Background

Friction observed while lead-driving epic 2821e177 (2026-07-03, session 2). The assign-then-claim sequence is exactly what container stewardship produces: a lead assigns an issue while its dependencies are still open (a full claim would exit 4 on the blocked in_progress transition), and later — once dependencies complete — wants to promote that assignment into a real claim and in_progress transition. That promotion rejects, and the operator falls back to `jit issue update --state in_progress`, which loses claim semantics (lease, claims.jsonl).

This concerns claim being non-idempotent at promotion time over an existing same-assignee assignment, which is a separate lifecycle point from claim's behavior at intake time on a dependency-blocked container.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `jit issue claim <id> <assignee>` on an issue already assigned to that same assignee proceeds rather than erroring — it records the lease and transitions to in_progress when unblocked. Covered by a test: assign X while dependencies are open, complete the dependencies, then claim as X and assert in_progress with a live lease.
- [hard] REQ-02: `jit issue claim <id> <assignee>` on an issue already assigned to a different assignee continues to fail as today. Covered by a test asserting the rejection.
